biography.education: B.A. Plan II Honors / Government, University of Texas at Austin (1996); J.D., George Washington University Law School (1999)
biography.background: Born in McAllen, Texas; raised in Brownsville; from Rio Grande Valley family. Started career as civil rights and union lawyer. Entered elected politics via Austin ISD school board in response to school closures. Elected to Texas House in 2016. Five-term legislator; known primarily for education policy and anti-corruption work. Announced governor candidacy October 15, 2025. Clear Democratic frontrunner: Andrew White withdrew and endorsed her; leads nearest remaining rival (Chris Bell) by ~40 percentage points as of early 2026. Statistically tied with Abbott in a February 2026 general election poll.
biography.fundraising: $1.3M raised as of early 2026 (compared to Abbott's ~$106M war chest)

campaignWebsite.notes: WebFetch tool unavailable; content gathered via WebSearch snippets from site pages

statedPositions.quote: Strengthen neighborhood schools by raising teacher pay, stopping the onslaught of standardized tests, and rooting out waste in Abbott's voucher scam.
statedPositions.notes: Central campaign theme; led House Democrats defeating vouchers for four consecutive sessions. Now explicitly committed to repealing the 2025 ESA voucher program as governor.

statedPositions.quote: Expand Medicaid to ensure every Texan has access to affordable, high-quality care.
statedPositions.notes: Explicit Medicaid expansion commitment. Does not state single-payer or public option in 2026 campaign; framing is Medicaid expansion within current structure. Note: in 2019 she pledged to carry the Healthy Texas Act (Medicare-for-All style). 2026 is more moderate — Medicaid expansion only.

statedPositions.quote: Oppose big insurance and big drug companies that are putting profits over patients; private equity buying up doctors' offices, anesthesia, and X-ray machines to charge more for less care. Rein in out-of-control profiteers who are making healthcare more expensive.
statedPositions.notes: Supports government/regulatory intervention on healthcare pricing and corporate consolidation in medicine

statedPositions.quote: Steering the state's financial incentives toward the small businesses that drive job growth instead of major corporations that pile up profits.
statedPositions.notes: Anti-corporate-subsidy framing; redirecting public investment toward small business vs. multinational corporations. Also: 'scrubbing the state budget, with priority on rooting out no-bid contracts and grift to find more money for public education.'

statedPositions.quote: While multi-national corporations post record profits, Texans are paying more for groceries, housing, utilities, insurance, and so much more. Texas needs leaders who are willing to take on the corporate greed that is making life increasingly unaffordable for working families.
statedPositions.notes: General affordability framing; specific housing policy detail limited on campaign site. Separate legislative record (HB 3050 inclusionary zoning) provides more specific signal.

statedPositions.quote: Ensure every Texan has the freedom to organize on the job and build a better life. I'll stand with working Texans on the picket line, fight for the right to organize and ensure that working families have a real voice in the decisions that shape their lives.
statedPositions.notes: Explicit pro-labor organizing commitment; Texas is right-to-work state — this signals support for changing that framework. AFL-CIO and SEIU both endorsed. Career began as union lawyer.

statedPositions.quote: Hinojosa Calls on Abbott to Stop Facilitating Fatal ICE Operations. Another American has been shot and killed in the street by ICE in MN. Abbott has provided Texas land and state resources to support Trump's immigration crackdown, making the state a central hub for what legal advocates are calling an illegal operation. Children are being torn from their homes and sent to taxpayer-funded private prisons in TX run by Abbott's donors.
statedPositions.notes: Press release calling for ICE oversight and criticizing Abbott's Operation Lone Star facilitation. Frames enforcement as lawless, child-harmful, and driven by donor corruption.

statedPositions.quote: Hinojosa Calls for Release of Body Cam Footage After ICE Killing of San Antonio Man Was Hidden for a Year. Filed Public Information Act request demanding transparency and accountability for ICE operations in Texas.
statedPositions.notes: Transparency and accountability in law enforcement applied to federal ICE operations; used formal legal mechanism (PIA request)

keyVotes.notes: Led House Democrats' successful effort; directed new public school funding; teacher pay raises. Direct counter to vouchers — one of her signature legislative victories.

keyVotes.bill: ESA (Education Savings Account / Voucher) Program — Multiple sessions (87th, 88th, 89th Legislatures)

evidenceSummary.notes: Gina Hinojosa has a rich 9-year elected record (Austin ISD board 2012–2016, Texas House 2017–present) providing strong Tier 1 and Tier 2 evidence on most axes. Her governor campaign is largely an extension of her legislative identity with relatively little new policy detail beyond Medicaid expansion and ICE/immigration accountability. First-time candidate for statewide office; no statewide voting record. Primary gap areas: detailed housing supply/zoning policy beyond inclusionary zoning repeal, transportation infrastructure, and state tax structure specifics (partially irrelevant given Texas has no income tax). The labor union division (some Teamsters going to Abbott) is noteworthy context but does not change her policy positions. The Medicaid expansion vs. 2019 Medicare-for-All evolution should be flagged but scored on current position.
